name: Immunoglobulin G Subclass Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for IgG Subclass Deficiency

criteria.description: Serum IgG subclass levels below age-adjusted reference range
History of recurrent bacterial infections, especially respiratory tract infections
Impaired antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low IgG subclass levels with recurrent infections; supportive criteria such as normal total IgG and poor vaccine response strengthen diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of immunodeficiency and consideration of clinical context.

pathognomonic.notes: Common presenting symptom due to impaired mucosal immunity

common.notes: Complication of recurrent lower respiratory infections

occasional.notes: May occur due to impaired immune defense

rare.notes: Severe systemic infection in immunocompromised patients

laboratory: Reduced serum levels of one or more IgG subclasses (IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, IgG4)
Normal or near-normal total IgG levels
Impaired specific antibody responses to polysaccharide vaccines (e.g., pneumococcal vaccine)
Normal or mildly reduced total immunoglobulins (IgA, IgM)
imaging: Chest radiographs or CT showing bronchiectasis or recurrent pneumonia
genetic: No consistent monogenic cause identified; possible familial aggregation
other: Poor clinical response to standard antibiotic therapy
Improvement with immunoglobulin replacement therapy in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Low total IgG and other immunoglobulin isotypes
May have normal levels of other IgG subclasses
Rare and often associated with other immunodeficiencies

redFlags: Frequent severe bacterial infections requiring hospitalization
Development of bronchiectasis or chronic lung disease
Poor response to standard antibiotic therapy
references: Orange JS, Ballow M, Stiehm ER, et al.
